environment.isolation: One database, backend and web server per area (e2e_<area>); only gi-e2e-db and ports 18100–18299 used.

counting.rule: Every number is recounted from the case files. A case is counted once, under its kind (API or UI).
counting.prd: Cases tagged with several clauses (only in the tasks exploratory pass, for example "A6/B1") count under the first. prdAll keeps the full list.
counting.byPrdStatus: PASS = no FAIL and no BLOCKED among the cases (NOT_TESTED are shown separately). PARTIAL = some pass and some fail or are blocked. FAIL = none pass and some fail.
counting.byPrdOverlap: The A1–B3 rows count every area, including regression and migration. The Regression and Migration rows count those two areas again, so they overlap the clause rows.
counting.truncation: actual and evidence are cut at 1500 characters; the full text is in resultsFile.

discrepanciesWithTesterSummaries: tasks suite: the first tester reported 0 cases (file not yet written). The final tasks report and runs/final/tasks.json agree: 75 cases, 75 PASS (44 API, 31 UI).

This report uses the recorded file.

Every other area matches the tester summaries exactly.

byPrd.title: Triggers: a rule fires on create/update of a Customer, Invoice or Payment, or on a daily/weekly schedule
Conditions: filters over the entity's fields, combined with AND and OR
Actions: create a Task, Promise or Dispute, or send an Email; assignees/recipients by role-at-a-level
Placeholders ({{Customer.Name}}, {{Invoice.Balance}} …) in subject and body; a multi-holder role resolves to the primary
Durable execution: trigger publishes an event, a consumer acts; never slows or breaks the save; nothing lost; schedule or run from the UI
Tasks on a customer, invoice or payment: title, due date, status, assignees
Regions: one region per record; per-region rights (read/manage/none); per-region POC book; every figure region-scoped
Maker-checker: changes above a per-region threshold stay pending until someone else with the approval right approves; visible while pending
As-of reads: lists, reports and rule evaluation as of a date, including the region then and the approvals outstanding then
Existing features keep working with the new build (regression area, all its cases)
Upgrade of an existing database to this build (migration area, all its cases)

byPrd.title: Triggers: a rule fires on create/update of a Customer, Invoice or Payment, or on a daily/weekly schedule
Conditions: filters over the entity's fields, combined with AND and OR
Actions: create a Task, Promise or Dispute, or send an Email; assignees/recipients by role-at-a-level
Placeholders ({{Customer.Name}}, {{Invoice.Balance}} …) in subject and body; a multi-holder role resolves to the primary
Durable execution: trigger publishes an event, a consumer acts; never slows or breaks the save; nothing lost; schedule or run from the UI
Tasks on a customer, invoice or payment: title, due date, status, assignees
Regions: one region per record; per-region rights (read/manage/none); per-region POC book; every figure region-scoped
Maker-checker: changes above a per-region threshold stay pending until someone else with the approval right approves; visible while pending
As-of reads: lists, reports and rule evaluation as of a date, including the region then and the approvals outstanding then
Existing features keep working with the new build (regression area, all its cases)
Upgrade of an existing database to this build (migration area, all its cases)

decisions.decision: Email attachments from the record/customer are deferred (DESIGN §10.1); nothing built.
List rows show an "Awaiting approval" chip when a change is held, so a pending change is visible to everyone who can see the record.
When the caller cannot see a record's customer, Customer.* placeholders render empty with a warning instead of a 400.
Requeuing a dead run-by-hand event is refused (400) unless the caller owns the rule; retry it from its run instead.
A role used as a task assignee or email To/Cc goes to every active holder who can see the record; "resolves to the primary" applies to placeholders, the From role and the promise Collection POC.
An approval viewed as of a date hides any decision taken after that date; status stays live and statusAt gives the status then.
On the health card a dead run-by-hand event offers "Open runs" (Retry from the rule's Runs tab) instead of Requeue; the owner can still requeue through the API.
When dashboard figures from several region parts are merged, tied amounts sort by name (case-insensitive, then exact, then id); a single part keeps the database order.
A blank note and no note are the same value for approvals and conflict checks.
On upgrade, legacy automation rows the new code cannot read are copied to <table>_legacy and removed from the live table with a warning; tables are never dropped.

Extends the r1 rule: every row of a legacy automation table missing a required column is archived to <table>_legacy before the schema update runs; a half-migrated database repairs itself on the next boot.

The approval Changes table shows invoices by number, promises as "Promise of <amount> by <date>", lines as "<qty> × <product> at <price>", falls back to "invoice #id" etc., and omits empty id lists on a create.
blockedReason order: as-of view first, then "You no longer have access to this record", then the other reasons; losing sight of the record does not take away the right to decide.
As of a date, names in the Changes table are read as the records stood on that date, falling back to today's name and then "invoice #id"; the page is never refused.
A placeholder goes in at the caret or selection the field had when the placeholder button was pressed; a select-all caused only by focus returning is ignored; the caret ends after the token.

After a customer moves out, the old region's approvers keep the change without now-values ("You no longer have access to this record"); the old region's plain viewers lose it; as of a date, the record's region then decides.
If the change's record cannot be found (deleted, or not yet created at the as-of date), visibility falls back to the change's own region.

A change is visible to whoever can see its record now, judged in the record's own region (as of a date, the region then); the region it was asked in still governs maker, approver, threshold-setter and named-POC paths.

In the approvals list a change matches a region filter by the region it was asked in or by its record's region, so a moved change can appear under both; the regionId column still means the region it was asked in.
When the viewer cannot open the record, the approval page shows Record and Customer as plain text and hides "Open …", even for a book-scoped approver who might still see the customer.

knownLimitations.what: rt.openApp's path option is not kept, so the app boots to '/'
